versions.name: Boxwell Reservation

features.note: Six air-conditioned shower houses, each combining shower, toilet, and sink.
Thirty COPE obstacles, with a separate advanced course.
Brownsea, the camp's first-year camper program, run at the Beany Elam program area.
Catch-and-release fishing on the lake; no licence needed.
The Boxwell museum of Scouting heritage.
The skilled trades program is restricted to Scouts aged thirteen and over.
Canvas tent, cot, and mattress provided at each site.
An Olympic-size pool with two slides.
Open rappelling from the climbing tower.
A Scuba BSA experience taught at the pool.
The Parnell STEM Center, a standalone hands-on facility.
Skiing from the Pfeffer Boat Harbor.
Nine miles of shoreline on Old Hickory Lake, with a waterfront at each of the two camps.
Part of the Roy Grindstaff Skilled Trades Center, equipped with service bays and classroom space.

versions.summary: Middle Tennessee Council's Scouts BSA resident summer camp near Lebanon, Tennessee, encompassing Camps Craig and Stahlman, offering more than sixty merit badges alongside adventure activities.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence). Most features come from the council's linked Boxwell program guide, since the camp page itself carries mainly dates and forms; features cover the whole reservation, which contains Camps Stahlman, Craig, and the Parnell program area.
